name: Timothy M. Kennedy

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: LINKING FAMILY MEMBERS THROUGHOUT THE NEXUS APPLICATION PROCESS
statements.title: LINKING FAMILY MEMBERS THROUGHOUT THE NEXUS APPLICATION PROCESS
sentences: Every day, nearly 328,000 people cross the northern border, powering local economies and cementing the deep ties that bind us with our Canadian neighbors.

In western New York, seamless, smooth travel through customs and across the U.S.-Canada border can make all the difference, whether you are reporting to work, visiting family and friends, or making the kickoff at a Bills' game or puck drop at a Sabres game.

NEXUS, a joint trusted traveler program between the U.S. and Canada was created in 2000 to improve this kind of travel and to allow preapproved, vetted travelers expedited processing across the northern border with their NEXUS pass.
Unfortunately, families in northern border States face unique challenges when applying for or renewing NEXUS.
Parents must then schedule separate interviews for their children, requiring multiple trips to enrollment centers, often located far from their home.
In practice, this means families bear the burden of bureaucratic red tape, discouraging NEXUS enrollment, and stifling travel to and from Canada.
By allowing CBP to waive interviews where appropriate for children under 14, this legislation removes unnecessary hurdles to enrollment, keeping travel efficient and seamless.
Importantly, this bill maintains the safe, secure vetting processes that have underpinned NEXUS for over two decades.
Mr. Speaker, I rise in support of my bill, the NEXUS for families act.
I urge my colleagues to support this underlying legislation to improve, encourage, and simplify travel to and from Canada.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: CONDEMNING TRUMP'S TRADE WAR WITH CANADA
statements.title: CONDEMNING TRUMP'S TRADE WAR WITH CANADA
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise today to condemn President Trump's illogical trade war with Canada and juvenile executive order to rename Lake Ontario.

While my Democratic colleagues and I have introduced legislation to stop this nonsense, we are focused on the issues that actually matter: ending the affordability crisis fueled by Trump's erratic tariffs and reckless policies and stopping the most corrupt administration in American history.

Whether it is his endless war in Iran, gutting healthcare and nutritional assistance for millions of Americans, or a trade war with Canada, each manufactured crisis created by Trump shows just how self- interested, incompetent, and careless he truly is.

From communities like mine across the northern border, where ties to our Canadian neighbors run deep, through the interior and every other part of our great country, people simply cannot afford the increased costs of goods because of these tariffs.
In western New York, family members cross the border to visit one another, and businesses rely on efficient cross-border commerce.
Americans are bearing the consequences of this economic ambush as Trump's failed policies make life more expensive and less secure for working families across our Nation.
These tariffs are nothing more than a Trump tax, and American families are paying the price everywhere.
Mr. Speaker, in the meantime, let's stop Trump's tax, end these tariffs, and make life more affordable for the American people. ____________________
When voters put Democrats back into the majority this November, we will overturn these failed GOP policies, lower costs, end corruption, and restore the promise of the American Dream.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: LIBERTY AND JUSTICE FOR ALL
statements.title: LIBERTY AND JUSTICE FOR ALL
sentences: The Constitution does not permit government officials to act with impunity, to use violence without accountability, or to treat human life as disposable.
Mr. Shah Alam should be alive today, which is why I introduced the DHS Release Transparency Act to prevent tragedies like this.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: WEATHERIZING INFRASTRUCTURE IN THE NORTH AND TERRORISM EMERGENCY READINESS ACT OF 2025
statements.title: WEATHERIZING INFRASTRUCTURE IN THE NORTH AND TERRORISM EMERGENCY READINESS ACT OF 2025
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise in support of my bill, H.R. 3106, the Weatherizing Infrastructure in the North and Terrorism Emergency Readiness Act, also known as the WINTER Act.
That is why I introduced the WINTER Act, to strengthen our Homeland Security posture during extreme cold weather conditions and ensure that the Department of Homeland Security is prepared to respond.
I urge all of my colleagues to support this vital legislation.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: COMMEMORATING NATIONAL POLICE WEEK
statements.title: COMMEMORATING NATIONAL POLICE WEEK
sentences: Mr. Speaker, as we commemorate National Police Week, I rise today on behalf of a grateful western New York community and a grateful nation to mourn the passing of Buffalo Police Inspector Daniel E. Redmond, whom we lost on March 4, 2026, at the age of 86.
His son, Daniel, and daughter-in-law, Lissa, both became Buffalo police detectives.
His eldest grandson, John, currently serves as a Buffalo police officer.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: FOURTH ANNIVERSARY OF THE TOPS SUPERMARKET SHOOTING IN BUFFALO, NEW YORK
statements.title: FOURTH ANNIVERSARY OF THE TOPS SUPERMARKET SHOOTING IN BUFFALO, NEW YORK
sentences: Today is a difficult day for our community, for the people of western New York, and for our country, as we mourn those we lost due to this senseless act of racist gun violence.
Yet, the carnage on that day could have been far worse if it weren't for the heroic actions of Lieutenant Aaron Salter, Jr., a 30-year veteran of the Buffalo Police Department.

On the fourth anniversary of this tragedy in Buffalo, we must use this opportunity to advocate for the advancement of commonsense gun violence prevention legislation in the name of every single person we have lost because of a lack of it.

We must condemn acts of hateful, racist violence in all forms, and we must come together as Americans to ensure that our supermarkets, our places of worship, our schools, and everywhere else in our community are free from the scourge of gun violence.
We must enact a permanent assault weapons ban and make sure that military-grade body armor is only in the hands of our Armed Forces and law enforcement.
We must crack down on ghost guns, straw purchasing, and deadly accessories that turn handguns into semiautomatic weapons.
We must close the Charleston loophole.
We must strengthen our mental health support networks.
We must reaffirm our commitment to ending the gun violence epidemic that plagues this country once and for all.
Today, you will hear from Members of the Congressional Black Caucus and the Gun Violence Prevention Task Force.

My colleagues from all over the country will join me in honoring the victims of the Top Supermarket shooting, condemning racially motivated violence in all forms, and calling for an end to the gun violence epidemic that plagues this country.

As it occurred, I was with my family out of town when I received a call from Zeneta Everhart, then my director of diversity, equity, and inclusion in my New York State Senate office, who is now president pro tempore of the Buffalo Common Council, representing the Masten District.
Frantic phone calls to friends, family, colleagues in government, and law enforcement followed for me as we struggled to understand what had happened.
We saw an almost immediate call to action to enact gun violence prevention legislation at the State level in the New York State legislature just days later.

We demanded action federally, including when I joined Zeneta here on the Hill as she testified before the House, along with the son of Ruth Whitfield, another victim, former Buffalo Fire Commissioner Garnell Whitfield, and the families of the victims of the Uvalde massacre, which spurred the first Federal gun violence action in decades.

Under Councilwoman Everhart's leadership, Buffalo has established an Office of Gun Violence Prevention, showing that even in the face of Federal inaction, communities can still take charge of their own future.
Part of that change, as mentioned by my colleagues, is enacting gun violence prevention legislation.

This bill, which I am proud to co-lead with Congresswoman Grace Meng, bans the sale and ownership of enhanced body armor--hard-shell, military-grade, rifle-resistant body armor that was used to carry out the Tops mass shooting.
This is body armor that should only be in the hands of our military and law enforcement.
No civilian should have access to military-grade body armor, equipment that is designed for war, not our streets.

The Lieutenant Aaron Salter, Jr., Responsible Body Armor Possession Act ensures that no civilian can possess military-grade body armor ever again--armor that has been used in mass shootings across the United States: Sutherland Springs, Texas; Aurora, Colorado; Boulder, Colorado; San Bernardino, California; and Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.
Gun violence legislation can help stop mass shootings.

While gun violence legislation can help stop mass shootings, I believe, with every fiber of my being, that we cannot discuss May 14, 2022, without acknowledging the underlying cause--the scourge of white supremacy, a legacy of our Nation's original sin of slavery.
It remains with the Supreme Court's evisceration of the Voting Rights Act, allowing States to break up communities of color and silence their voices.
She was a longtime campaigner against gun violence, founding We Are Women Warriors with her friends Betty Jean Grant and Dr. Eva Doyle.
I want to thank the Congressional Black Caucus and the Gun Violence Prevention Task Force for joining in as well in commemorating this fourth anniversary of the Tops Friendly Markets massacre.
Today, we honor the victims and their families, and we urge this body to pass meaningful gun violence prevention legislation to ensure we live in a country free from tragedies like 5/14.
Our city, our State, our community, and our country mourn with them, but we are driven in their memory to do better for all of us and for future generations that we will never meet.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: CONDEMNING TRUMP'S ATTACKS ON POPE LEO XIV
statements.title: CONDEMNING TRUMP'S ATTACKS ON POPE LEO XIV

sentences: I choose to stand against Islamophobia, and I urge my colleagues and all Americans to do the same. ____________________

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: ICE SHOOTING OF RENEE NICOLE GOOD
statements.title: ICE SHOOTING OF RENEE NICOLE GOOD
sentences: Donald Trump and Kristi Noem have created an Immigration and Customs Enforcement with no oversight, no chain of command, no standards, and no restraint.
From pepper-spraying children to deploying armed masked agents in the neighborhood raids with zero oversight, ICE has become a rogue agency operating above the law.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROTECTING EDUCATION FOR CHILDREN WITH DISABILITIES
statements.title: PROTECTING EDUCATION FOR CHILDREN WITH DISABILITIES
sentences: Yet, this anniversary comes at a time when the Trump administration continues its systematic efforts to eliminate the Department of Education, gut the Office of Special Education Programs, and undermine IDEA, a landmark law that fundamentally changed how we educate children with disabilities.

IDEA part C, a Federal program closely intertwined the Medicaid, provides early intervention from birth to age 3, oftentimes the difference between a child meeting developmental milestones or falling behind.

I am here to remind the American people that the President's shameless assault on early intervention and Medicaid paints a grim picture for the future of special education and for the future of millions of children.
Early intervention care alters the course of a child's life for the better, dramatically improves health and educational outcomes, and gives working families the support they desperately need.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: FACING TAX CREDIT EXPIRATION AND HEALTHCARE AFFORDABILITY CRISIS
statements.title: FACING TAX CREDIT EXPIRATION AND HEALTHCARE AFFORDABILITY CRISIS
sentences: Mr. Speaker, with just 24 days left before open enrollment closes in New York State and with millions of New Yorkers facing massive premium hikes, I rise today in outrage.
When healthcare is out of reach, outcomes get worse, costs go up, and working families pay the price.
That is exactly what is happening right now because Republicans have allowed the enhanced Affordable Care Act premium tax credits to expire.
When the Affordable Care Act was enacted in 2014, it made health insurance more affordable and expanded access to care, putting healthcare within reach for millions of Americans.

After years of trying to undermine the Affordable Care Act, congressional Republicans chose on December 31 to let these lifesaving premium tax credits expire, even over the objections from Members of their own party.
Enrollment will plummet, and millions of Americans will lose or forego coverage entirely.
Young people in communities of color will be hardest hit, reversing years of progress and 4 consecutive years of Affordable Care Act enrollment, a record high.
As this is happening at a moment when the cost-of-living crisis is already crushing working families, the people of this country are saying enough is enough.
They pushed through the largest healthcare cuts in U.S. history, gutting Medicaid, Medicare, and the Affordable Care Act by more than $1 trillion.

Now, instead of fixing the damage, Republican leadership is once again choosing to turn its back on families by letting these premium tax credits expire, a lifeline millions of Americans rely on to stay insured.

That is why Democrats have forced a vote to extend these credits this week, and that is why I intend to vote ``yes.'' Healthcare should not depend on your ZIP Code, your job title, or the size of your paycheck.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: JANUARY 6 ATTACK
statements.title: JANUARY 6 ATTACK
sentences: In the days and weeks following the attack, we lost five of those police officers, those brave heroes.
They have been charged with assaulting police officers, making terrorist threats, and preying on children.
Mr. Speaker, first, I will recognize the CBC and Chairwoman Clarke and Representatives Clyburn and Hoyer for hosting this Special Order hour.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: ENACTING REAL CHANGE FOR GUN VIOLENCE
statements.title: ENACTING REAL CHANGE FOR GUN VIOLENCE
sentences: Once again, we have seen hatred rear its ugly head in the form of gun violence, this time with 2 students murdered and 9 more injured at Brown, and 15 murdered and dozens injured in Sydney.
We ensured that military-grade body armor stays only in the hands of law enforcement and our Armed Forces.
We implemented enhanced red flag laws and universal background checks.
In the United States, for far too long, some have treated gun violence as a part of life.

I implore this body to join me in supporting the assault weapons ban; universal background checks; stronger red flag laws; ending gun trafficking across State lines; and, among others, my bill, the Lieutenant Aaron Salter, Jr., Responsible Body Armor Possession Act.
I pray that our country sees the light and enacts real, substantive change that will end the scourge of gun violence across our Nation. ____________________
My Democratic colleagues and I reject that.

We refuse to accept a reality in which our schools, our houses of worship, our movie theaters, our grocery stores, our government offices, our workplaces, our parades, our malls, and our nightclubs are treated as if they haven't been the scenes of horrific, deadly attacks.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: HEALTHCARE PROFESSIONAL DEGREES
statements.title: HEALTHCARE PROFESSIONAL DEGREES
sentences: I took on that debt because I wanted to build a better future for my family and because I wanted to help people as a healthcare practitioner.

This means fewer nurses at the bedside, fewer therapists helping patients recover, fewer specialists serving rural communities, and fewer mental health providers at a time when this Nation is desperate for them.

Not only will healthcare professionals be impacted but teachers, architects, accountants, engineers, and many other professionals who will lose the ability to finance their education through reliable, flexible Federal loans, pushing them instead into the arms of predatory private lenders and adding to the mountain of debt that our students already endure.
The United States also needs tens of thousands of new mental health professionals and rehabilitation providers annually.
Under this thoughtless Republican rule, if you want to save lives, prepare to drown in debt.
As the only occupational therapist in Congress, I will not sit idly by while Trump and congressional Republicans sabotage the very workforce that keeps this Nation alive.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: VETERANS' COMPENSATION COST-OF-LIVING ADJUSTMENT ACT OF 2025
statements.title: VETERANS' COMPENSATION COST-OF-LIVING ADJUSTMENT ACT OF 2025
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise in support of S. 2392, the Veterans' Compensation Cost-of-Living Adjustment Act of 2025.
That is exactly why we need the Veterans' Compensation Cost-of-Living Adjustment Act.

By adjusting the rate of these benefits to keep pace with inflation and align with annual increases from the Social Security Administration, our veterans will not have to choose between medication, housing, groceries, or utility bills.
I will proudly be voting to support this legislation, and I urge all of my colleagues to do the same.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF SENATE AMENDMENT TO H.R. 5371, CONTINUING APPROPRIATIONS AND EXTENSIONS ACT, 2026
statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF SENATE AMENDMENT TO H.R. 5371, CONTINUING APPROPRIATIONS AND EXTENSIONS ACT, 2026
sentences: I have heard from so many who are desperate for a lifeline, like Iris, a mom in Buffalo, who is worried about how she will keep her kids' healthcare insurance; or Andy, a nursing home resident in Tonawanda, who relies on Medicaid to get the services he needs; or the kids at Bornhava, a special needs school where I provided therapy, who depend on early intervention services.

Mr. Speaker, as the Representative of western New York, where so many people in my community, like others across the country, are already struggling to afford healthcare, I urge my colleagues to reject this disgraceful bill.
I will be voting ``no,'' and I urge all my colleagues to do the same.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF SENATE AMENDMENT TO H.R. 1, ONE BIG BEAUTIFUL BILL ACT
statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF SENATE AMENDMENT TO H.R. 1, ONE BIG BEAUTIFUL BILL ACT
sentences: I know exactly what it means to cut $1 trillion from Medicare, Medicaid, and the Affordable Care Act, which is exactly what this big, ugly bill does.
Giving billionaires a tax break won't make us any richer.
Mr. Speaker, I ask unanimous consent to amend the rule to make in order the amendment at the desk that protects against any cuts to Medicaid and SNAP.

Mr. Speaker, I urge my Republican colleagues to stand up; grow a spine; stop bowing down to your king, Donald Trump; represent your constituents like you were elected to do; and vote ``no'' on this horrible, big, ugly bill.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: ECONOMIC HARM OF TARIFFS IN NEW YORK STATE
statements.title: ECONOMIC HARM OF TARIFFS IN NEW YORK STATE
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise today to sound the alarm on the economic harm President Trump's reckless tariff policies continue to cause across this country, especially in my district of western New York.
Make no mistake, Mr. Speaker, these tariffs are taxes, and they are being paid not by foreign governments or corporations but by working families and small businesses at home.
Mr. Speaker, whether you call it tariff roulette or a trade tug-of- war, it has created instability that has devastated communities across the country.
As a Representative for a northern border community, I can tell you firsthand, Mr. Speaker, that this trade war is hurting Americans.
In our community, we have already seen a serious drop in Canadian visitors who for decades have driven across the border to support our local economy.
New York exports more than $17 billion in goods and services across the border each year, supporting tens of thousands of jobs.
Disrupting that trade through politically motivated tariffs puts those jobs at risk.
We need stability and support for working families, not another round of trade retaliation disguised as strategy.
It is time to reject this billionaire's first agenda and fight for an economy that works for everyone.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS
statements.title: EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS
sentences: If the Republican majority in Congress allow this administration to dismantle the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, defund the National Weather Service, and hollow out FEMA, then they are failing every family that depends on those agencies to survive the next natural disaster.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DEFENDING SOCIAL SERVICES AND PROGRAMS
statements.title: DEFENDING SOCIAL SERVICES AND PROGRAMS
sentences: President Trump, unelected billionaire Elon Musk, and Secretary Robert Kennedy are more concerned with cutting services and pushing an antiscience agenda than they are with supporting and improving our healthcare system.

Mr. Speaker, I urge this body, Democrats and Republicans, to stand up for our healthcare heroes, invest in breakthroughs that millions of lives are depending on, and restore the funding and workforce our Nation's healthcare system depends upon.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: SOCIAL SECURITY IS NOT A GIVEAWAY
statements.title: SOCIAL SECURITY IS NOT A GIVEAWAY
sentences: That promise is called Social Security, and it is a solemn promise we must keep.

Yet, from Elon Musk accessing private beneficiary data to Trump's handpicked Acting Commissioner declaring living recipients to be deceased in order to claw back their benefits, Social Security is under fire.
Starting next week, a new rule will create further barriers, requiring in-person identity verification for those who are unable to register online.
Social Security is not a giveaway.
Without Social Security, nearly 22 million Americans--many of them seniors on a fixed income or people with disabilities--will be plunged into poverty overnight.
In my district alone, over 167,000 people rely on Social Security benefits to pay their bills, put food on the table, and afford their prescriptions.

Despite the incredible progress we have made as a Nation to keep people out of poverty, President Trump and Elon Musk are rolling back the clock in order to give tax cuts to billionaires and the ultrarich.
Elon Musk even called Social Security the biggest Ponzi scheme of all time.
Congress must reject the administration's attempt to weaken Social Security.
We need to fight tooth and nail against those who want to raise the retirement age, reduce benefits, or privatize this program for the benefit of corporations and the ultrarich.
Instead, we should be strengthening Social Security to protect this vital safety net and fighting for an America where working people get to retire with dignity.
President Trump needs to keep his hands off Social Security.
Mr. Speaker, I rise today in strong opposition to President Trump and Elon Musk's attacks on the safety nets that countless western New Yorkers and people across the country have earned and need.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: MOURNING THE LOSS OF MICHAEL "MICKEY" HARMON AND JORDAN CELOTTO
statements.title: MOURNING THE LOSS OF MICHAEL "MICKEY" HARMON AND JORDAN CELOTTO
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise with a heavy heart to join Buffalo's LGBTQ+ and arts communities in mourning the tragic and senseless deaths of Michael ``Mickey'' Harmon and Jordan Celotto.
Mickey's vision and skill, in partnership with his fellow artist and activist Ari Moore, told the story of Buffalo's LGBTQ+ heroes on a mural in the heart of Buffalo's gay nightlife neighborhood.
Mickey thrived as a leader in Buffalo's LGBTQ+ and arts communities.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: TSA COMMUTING FAIRNESS ACT
statements.title: TSA COMMUTING FAIRNESS ACT
sentences: Transportation Security officers, or TSOs, inspect travelers as they move through checkpoints; Federal air marshals ensure in-flight security; and canine handlers enhance the system's security.
Many employees find that the housing they can afford is far from airports, lending to long commutes with limited public transit options and heavy traffic.

My bill, the TSA Commuting Fairness Act, will help improve conditions for these civil servants by directing TSA to conduct a feasibility study on using mobile location data to allow employees to clock in for work upon arrival at the airport transit stops instead of when they reach that security checkpoint.
Mr. Speaker, I rise in support of my bill, H.R. 862, the TSA Commuting Fairness Act.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DEFENSE OF DEDICATED FEDERAL PUBLIC SERVANTS
statements.title: DEFENSE OF DEDICATED FEDERAL PUBLIC SERVANTS
sentences: Hardworking families in my district and people across the country are beginning to see this initiative for what it really is: a sham perpetrated by President Trump and run by an unelected billionaire, the richest person in the world, who has no idea how our government operates or what our public servants do for our communities.
Trump and Musk's goal is to undermine people's faith in public services, gain access to sensitive government data, and ultimately give away trillions of dollars in tax cuts for the rich.

Last week, I met with union leaders who are representing our Federal workforce, including the American Federation of Government Employees, National Nurses United, the National Association of Letter Carriers, the American Postal Workers Union, and the Western New York Area Labor Federation.

I am deeply grateful for their work to empower our Federal workforce: our air traffic controllers, veteran healthcare practitioners, Social Security benefit experts, and so many more who provide the services and assistance hardworking families in our communities deserve and need.

Union leaders on the front lines painted a picture in which our Federal workers are living in fear of wrongful firings, receiving intimidating emails that are causing mass confusion, and receiving unclear directives from an administration that has no interest in the rule of law.
They help our parents and grandparents receive the Social Security that they have earned and rely on.
Service-disabled veterans are among the 8,500 Federal employees in my district alone being attacked and dismissed for being DEI hires.

Meanwhile, unelected billionaire Elon Musk is celebrating on the world stage with a chain saw in his hand, bragging about the degrading treatment of our public servants, with no regard for the taxpayers who will suffer as a result because they cannot get the services that they rely on.
We won't let him take a chain saw to our Federal workforce without a fight.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: THREE-YEAR ANNIVERSARY OF RUSSIA'S BRUTAL ATTACK ON UKRAINE
statements.title: THREE-YEAR ANNIVERSARY OF RUSSIA'S BRUTAL ATTACK ON UKRAINE
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise today to support our ally, Ukraine, and speak up against the grave threat the Trump administration's support for Russia poses to democracy at home and abroad.
Yesterday marked 3 years since Russia's unprovoked and brutal invasion of Ukraine, a sovereign nation.
We have since witnessed incredible bravery from the Ukrainian soldiers on the front lines to the families who have endured unimaginable loss yet continue to fight for their homeland.
I stood arm in arm with western New York's Ukrainian community in Niagara Square, designated Ukraine Freedom Square, just outside Buffalo City Hall days after Russia's invasion.
What I said then is just as true today: The United States of America must always stand with Ukraine against Russian aggression.

Buffalo is known as the City of Good Neighbors, and that spirit has been evident in the way our community has opened its doors to Ukrainian refugees, providing shelter, education, and hope for a better future.
Members of this body, both Democrats and Republicans alike, understand that this is not just Ukraine's fight.
That is why this body has come together on numerous occasions to pass legislation to help the people of Ukraine resist the Russian invasion and defend their homeland.
We continue to do this because we know that if Russia succeeds, it sets a dangerous precedent for dictators around the world, and it threatens the security of our NATO allies.

When the President of the United States chooses to spread the same false Russian propaganda as Vladimir Putin, absolving Russia for its responsibility of starting the war and defaming the democratically elected President of our ally, we should have the courage to stand up and call it what it is: a bald-faced lie.
It is shameful when we, the shining city upon a hill, as President Reagan put it, oppose a United Nations resolution condemning Russia and supporting Ukraine.
The only other countries to oppose this resolution were Russia, North Korea, and Belarus, all dictatorships.
Turning our back on Ukraine goes against everything Americans have fought and died for since we declared our independence from a monarch in England.
Supporting Russian aggression against Ukraine sends a dangerous message to our allies around the world: The United States is no longer a reliable friend.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: ELON MUSK-DOGE THREATS TO GOVERNMENT
statements.title: ELON MUSK-DOGE THREATS TO GOVERNMENT
sentences: People in my district and others across the country do not want an unelected billionaire dismantling our government for parts and raking in profits in the process.

In my district alone, there are 8,500-plus Federal employees, including those at the Buffalo VA Medical Center, the Social Security Administration, the Niagara Falls Air Reserve Station, and many, many other agencies that help our communities each and every day.
We can't protect the privacy of millions of Americans if Elon Musk has access to private taxpayer data, including that of Social Security recipients, Medicare beneficiaries, and taxpayers.
This is an unelected billionaire who has made those billions in large part from taxpayer-funded government contracts.
We must continue to fight for the rights and well- being of hardworking families and put people over billionaire profit.
We can't allow an individual who prioritizes profits above all and cozies up to adversaries like China and Russia to make decisions for the American people.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: ADDRESSING THE HACK OF U.S. TREASURY PAYMENT SYSTEMS
statements.title: ADDRESSING THE HACK OF U.S. TREASURY PAYMENT SYSTEMS
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise in strong support of the Taxpayer Data Protection Act.
The American people deserve a government that protects their most sensitive personal information instead of one that allows an unelected billionaire to rifle through it.
Under this guise of efficiency, however, this administration has handed over Social Security and Medicare beneficiaries' private data to a billionaire with no oversight and endless ways to profit.

It is about consolidating power in the hands of the few at the expense of hardworking families, at the expense of the 167,000 western New Yorkers in my district who rely on Social Security benefits and the 335,000 taxpayers in my district who file tax returns every year.
The Taxpayer Data Protection Act would protect any unelected billionaire from having unlawful access to private and sensitive data.
This bill would restore proper safeguards for the Treasury and ensure that no administration can hand over control of taxpayer data to an unelected, unvetted, and unqualified billionaire.
Mr. Speaker, we will not stand by as our institutions are auctioned off for the rich to profit at the expense of hardworking families.
I urge my colleagues on both sides of the aisle to join me in defending the well-being and security of the people we were all elected to represent.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: SUPPORTING FEDERAL WORKERS
statements.title: SUPPORTING FEDERAL WORKERS
sentences: They process veterans' benefits, ensure Social Security checks go out on time, make Medicare payments to our seniors' physicians, ensure our air and water are clean, keep our Nation safe, and much, much more.
Yet, right now, they are under attack from a President who has outsourced his own power to a billionaire hell-bent on dismantling our government to serve his own greed.
They do not want an unelected billionaire who, I might add, has made billions off taxpayer-funded contracts to actively weaken our government.
They do not want an unelected billionaire to create a system where the rules don't apply to him and democracy takes a back seat to his own profits.
They do not want an unelected billionaire to attack our Federal workers whose love for our country keeps our communities safe and our society functioning.

This is an attack on Federal workers that will allow those at the highest levels of our government and their billionaire buddies to exploit the concerns of our constituents, take power away from the people, and enrich themselves at the expense of hardworking families in America.
As a member of the Labor Caucus, I am proud to support the public servants who dedicate their lives to keeping our country running, including the 8,500 Federal employees who call my district home.
We will not stand by while they buck the rule of law to dismantle the very institutions that protect hardworking families, seniors, veterans, and our democracy.
America's civil service is a pillar of our society, and we will defend it.
We will fight for your jobs, your dignity, and the services that millions of Americans rely on.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: BORN-ALIVE ABORTION SURVIVORS PROTECTION ACT
statements.title: BORN-ALIVE ABORTION SURVIVORS PROTECTION ACT
sentences: Six weeks before my wife gave birth, we went for an ultrasound and received the worst news imaginable.
As we faced one of our darkest days as a family, the last thing we needed was legislation that served to stand between the health of my wife, unborn child, and the future of our family.

If this bill had been law, doctors would have been required to whisk Brigid away from us, inhumanely poke and prod our baby girl with tubes, needles, and IVs, causing her needless pain, suffering, and torture.

Our government has no business intruding on a family's deeply personal medical decisions, yet the Supreme Court's Dobbs decision has opened the floodgate for States to rob women and families of the ability to make healthcare choices with their doctors, including the very difficult choice to access safe, legal, and oftentimes medically necessary abortions.
Madam Speaker, they are now using this bill, built on a despicable lie rooted in neither medicine nor science, to restrict access to abortion nationwide.
Madam Speaker, I rise today to oppose H.R. 21, an assault on women's healthcare and fundamental rights.
Madam Speaker, today, I will vote ``no'' on H.R. 21, and I urge my colleagues to do the same.
